Cohoes man heads to prison for stealing over $4M from employer to buy crack cocaine

Michael Goot WNYT
September 9, 2026 - 2:32 PM
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:31
Instaread

ALBANY, N.Y. (WNYT) — A Cohoes man was sent to prison after prosecutors said he stole more than $4 million from his former employer in Albany County’s biggest grand larceny case.

Albany County District Attorney Lee C. Kindlon said Kevin Stevens, 62, was sentenced Wednesday morning by Judge Christopher Maier to four to 12 years in state prison. Kindlon said Stevens pleaded guilty to first-degree grand larceny and first-degree identity theft, and was also ordered to pay full restitution to A.E. Rosen Electrical Co., Inc.

According to Kindlon, Stevens was the company’s chief financial officer and began the theft in January 2017. Prosecutors said he used company fuel and fleet cards to buy gift cards without permission, traded them for crack cocaine and also wrote himself unauthorized checks.

The District Attorney’s Office said Stevens used the company owner’s personal information on fraudulent financial forms to hide the fleet card use. Prosecutors said he also created false ledgers and financial reports for the company’s accounting firm, which then issued annual financial statements based on those false records.

Stevens expressed report for his crimes and the “pain and utter confusion” they caused.

“The crimes I committed were all for the sole purpose of fueling my addiction. It completely changed the man I was,” he said.

An investigation by New York State Police said Stevens stole $4,206,269 from A.E. Rosen between Jan. 24, 2017 and Jan. 23, 2025. The district attorney said the case is the largest grand larceny prosecution ever handled by the office.

Before sentencing, Stevens apologized to the company, former co-workers, family and friends, according to the release. He also told Maier he planned to become an alcohol and substance abuse counselor after his release.

“I’m encouraged by the fact that you have already taken steps to address your behavior,” Maier said.

Assistant District Attorney Matt Peluso, chief of the Financial Crimes Bureau, prosecuted the case.

A.E. Rosen has filed a lawsuit against Cumberland Farms, alleging that the company should have flagged the amount of cards he was purchasing at the store — often multiple times per day at the same or nearby locations, according to the lawsuit. He spent as much as over $2,000 at one location.

The lawsuit said his buying was “wholly inconsitent with legitimate retail customer behavior.”

A.E. Rosen is seeking $2.46 million in damages.

NewsChannel 13 has reached out to Cumberland Farms for comment.
